meta.description: Predicts community functional POTENTIAL from 16S amplicon ASVs with PICRUSt2 (or q2-picrust2) by phylogenetic interpolation of reference-genome gene content - EPA-ng placement, gappa, castor hidden-state prediction of KO/EC/Pfam copy number, 16S copy-number normalization, and MinPath MetaCyc/KEGG pathways - gated by the NSTI quality index.
meta.reaudit_role: third independent agent (different from original auditor and fixer)

scientific_integrity.detail: Every number in this re-audit traces to a fresh, independently executed run by this re-auditor (own PICRUSt2 2.6.3 pipeline run from a fresh biom export, own R ALDEx2/MaAsLin2/LinDA runs on a new gut-vs-left-palm comparison), not reused figures from the original audit or the fix log.

practice_boundaries.detail: No diagnostic or prescriptive medical conclusions; unaffected by the fix.

methodological_ground.detail: Circularity and activity-claim guidance (Inputs 6-7) is unchanged by the fix and re-verified by inspection to still correctly steer an agent away from both fallacies.

code_usability.detail: Cleanly PASS this time: the pre-fix audit had to argue PASS despite a real, reproducible FileNotFoundError because SKILL.md's Version Compatibility note told the agent to self-heal. Post-fix, the mandatory NSTI snippet was run verbatim (only the output path substituted) against a completely independent fresh PICRUSt2 run and completed without error, reproducing the exact NSTI numbers (mean 0.077, median 0.001, 3/751 dropped) three separate times now across the original audit, the fix log, and this re-audit.

functional_suitability.note: The unsubstantiated '/ITS' claim is removed from the frontmatter and usage-guide.md (verified via diff); the two real factual/output-format errors found on execution (NSTI filename, biom-TSV format) are both corrected and independently re-verified by fresh execution. Not full marks: Appropriateness/Completeness were already strong pre-fix and are unchanged.

reliability.note: Common Errors table now covers all three real failure modes independently re-verified this pass (NSTI filename, hard-abort vs near-empty split, biom-TSV comment-line trap), each with an accurate fix. Recoverability substantially improved: an agent following the docs in order now avoids the crash instead of hitting a blind FileNotFoundError. Not full marks: no bundled fixture/expected-output test harness exists to catch a future regression automatically.

performance_context.note: The Input Format Trap callout now appears immediately after the pipeline invocation and before any command is run, preventing the ~10-30 minute wasted-compute scenario this re-audit independently reproduced when the warning is ignored.

agent_usability.note: Output file specs are now verified accurate against a real, independently-executed PICRUSt2 2.6.3 run (combined_/bac_/arc_ prefixes all confirmed present and correctly named). Not full marks: Mode D hybrid complexity (CLI + Python + R across two languages and an external tool chain) remains inherently demanding regardless of the fix.

human_usability.note: The hardcoded, version-drifted filename that was 'the opposite of forgiving' pre-fix is corrected and confirmed forgiving in practice: this re-auditor ran the mandatory snippet verbatim with zero manual correction needed.

recommendations.title: LinDA crashes outright on predicted-pathway tables with near-zero-count features under default (no) prevalence filtering
recommendations.problem: Discovered independently while adding LinDA as a third CoDA tool for a new comparison (gut vs left palm): MicrobiomeStat::linda() throws 'contrasts can be applied only to factors with 2 or more levels' and aborts the ENTIRE run (not just the offending feature) when prev.filter = 0.0 (no prevalence filtering, the natural default since SKILL.md's DA guidance says nothing about pre-filtering) and at least one of the 503 predicted pathways has fewer than 2 nonzero values across the compared groups. Root-caused with a minimal repro (run/06_linda_crash_diagnostic.R): prev.filter = 0.1 fixes it completely (469/503 features fit cleanly).
recommendations.root_cause: SKILL.md names LinDA as one of four CoDA tools an agent might pick for the '>=2 CoDA tools, report intersection' guidance, but gives no caveat about prevalence-filtering near-zero predicted pathways before running it -- unlike the ALDEx2 features-as-rows warning, which IS present.
recommendations.fix: Add a one-line caveat next to the CoDA-tools guidance: filter near-zero-prevalence pathways (e.g. prev.filter/min_prevalence >= 0.1) before running LinDA on a predicted pathway table, since an unfiltered near-zero feature can abort the entire run rather than failing gracefully per-feature. This is out of this skill's own shipped code (no LinDA example lives here) -- also worth flagging for the differential-abundance skill, which owns LinDA's actual example code and may have the same gap.
